dod_legs.note: The report names the collision reproduced (explicit target 'session:4' after index 4 was occupied) and the state it strands (board assignment durable, clones + wrapper present, no pane), and describes the after-state (append/free-slot allocation of the task-named window with index 4 still occupied, plus the recovery print). The drill fixture that produces this is in the patch: hive-tooling-drill.sh:150-159 occupies index 4 and asserts the explicit re-target fails; :191-192 assert the task-named window was allocated anyway and the occupied index was left untouched. The report is explicit that the end-to-end drill could not be executed here ('stopped at tmux session creation with Operation not permitted ... before any drill assertion ran'), which is the order's own named-risk path ('the report says what was asserted instead of faking coverage') and matches the rubric's out-of-scope carve-out. Wording note only, not a defect: the first sentence of 'How verified' is past-tense in a way that reads as an observation, but the disclosure three sentences later removes any chance of a reader being misled.

docs/omegahive_recovery_runbook.md gains section 1.1 'Half-launched task after a tmux window failure' (candidate.patch:9-27). Recognition: the stderr string 'window creation failed after board seeding', task confirmed 'assigned', clone + wrapper present, no pane. Why relaunch is wrong: 'Do not re-run hive-launch; it will refuse the already-assigned task and cannot repair this state' - accurate against hive-launch:121-122, which dies on assigned|blocked|in_progress. How to finish by hand: run the printed 'tmux new-window -a' (or the 'new-session' alternative), verify the window name, use the filled kickoff, emit task.accepted through the wrapper. It also draws the boundary against task.reassigned, which is the pre-existing dead-worker path.

hive-launch:135-138 refuses a session window already named for the task and now names the recovery path: '... (the pane is the registry); recover via the existing pane or WORKER.md §Launch, never create a second window'. The guard sits before provisioning and before any board emit (clones start at :162-165), so the refusal creates neither a second window nor orphaned state. Covered by hive-tooling-drill.sh:403-407, which asserts both the message and that nothing was provisioned.

hive-launch:253 now issues 'tmux new-window -a -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" -n "$TASK" ...' - the launcher supplies only the session and the window name, never an index. '-a' is documented append/free-slot semantics (inserts at the next index up, moving windows up if necessary), so it cannot raise 'index N in use'; this is the candidate form the order itself names. The no-session branch (:259) is unchanged new-session, which never targets an index.

Both window-creation calls are wrapped (hive-launch:252-264); on failure manual_recovery() prints to stderr the exact 'new-window -a' command (and a 'new-session' alternative), shell-quoted via printf %q including the multi-line kickoff, plus the remaining WORKER.md §Launch steps, the 'do not re-run hive-launch' instruction, and the full filled kickoff between BEGIN/END markers, then exits 1. Existing refusal paths are untouched. The order requires the ordering choice and rationale be stated in 'To operate'; the report does so (seed-then-pane retained deliberately, because the assignment is durable and the index is never chosen).
